details.mechanismOrProperty: A temporary handle, subscription, lock, cursor, lease, or stream needs an owner whose lifetime includes its use and whose cleanup runs on terminal paths.
details.scenarioApplication: A photo-archive curation tool: A metadata merge opens two asset locks and a temporary merge record. The merge operation owns all three; a conflict or cancellation releases both locks and discards the temporary record without changing the accepted asset. Close both acquired locks and discard the temporary record on conflict/cancel; publish only the completed merge.
details.errorCorrection: A conflict means the merge did not commit and should no longer retain either lock. The temporary record is not accepted metadata and must not be visible as the asset's current description. The merge has ended, so a background task cannot safely inherit locks it did not acquire.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The nearest alternative is keep the first lock held while asking a curator to resolve the conflict later. It can seem convenient for retry or reuse, but the prompt names which operation still owns the resource and when that operation ends.
details.transfer: Separate durable domain state from temporary resources. Keep each temporary resource within the operation that acquired it, release on success/failure/cancel, and transfer ownership only at an explicit successful handoff.
